name: Permis de Sejour (Employer-Sponsored)

requirements.blocker_text: Direction de l'Immigration et de l'Emigration (DIE): a foreigner working in Haiti applies for the SAME general permis de sejour that covers all non-tourist foreign residents -- Haiti does not run a separate labor-ministry work-permit process layered on top, unlike several other countries in this dataset. The application requires an employment letter from the employer/sponsor guaranteeing the worker's support and repatriation, the employer's business license (or an NGO's operating authorization), a passport photocopy, a medical certificate under 30 days old, two color photos, a copy of the most recent entry boarding pass, a French-translated birth certificate, a criminal record from the country of origin, and a Haitian bank attestation showing at least 7,500 gourdes (~$200). A 5,000-gourde fee is paid to the public treasury after an interview and completed application form. The DIE page does not specify the permit's validity period or renewal cycle.
requirements.fix_path: Have the employer issue a support/repatriation guarantee letter and provide its business license, then file the permis de sejour application with the DIE, including the medical certificate, bank attestation, and criminal record.

evidence_required.document: Employer/sponsor letter guaranteeing support and repatriation
Employer's business license or NGO authorization
Criminal record from country of origin

outcome.duration_length: not specified by the source; permis de sejour, presumed renewable

sources.title: Direction de l'Immigration et de l'Emigration, Ministere de l'Interieur et des Collectivites Territoriales (official government portal) -- permis de sejour requirements, documents, fee

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Haiti). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- hard requirement sourced directly to Haiti's own immigration authority, tier 1 -- a genuinely solid government-hosted source despite Haiti's severe current instability (extensive gang control of Port-au-Prince and a transitional government as of this build), worth noting since several other countries in this dataset had far worse government-fetch failure rates than Haiti did. MARQUEE STRUCTURAL FINDING for this country's residence-based files (see ht_investor_residence.json, ht_family_reunification.json): Haiti runs ONE unified permis de sejour process for essentially all non-tourist foreign residents -- there is no separate labor-ministry work-authorization step, no distinct investor-visa category, and no distinct family-reunification track; the SAME document checklist applies, varying only in which 'purpose' document is substituted (an employer's letter here; a business owner's own registration for ht_investor_residence.json; a family sponsor's guarantee for ht_family_reunification.json). This is a more consolidated system than either Mali or Niger, both built earlier in this dataset, which at least layered a separate labor-ministry step on top of the residence card. citizenship_after_months (60) reflects the standalone naturalization track's standard 5-year threshold (see ht_citizenship_naturalisation.json), not a permit-specific automatic conversion. family_can_work left null: not addressed by the source.
